alkapoan_bargin.m: Yeah, sure, twenty-five thousand and I take a couple of your fingers too?

alkapoan_lie_wh_10.m: You want the house for yourself? Now that is interesting. Most people shy away from that cursed glow, but I can see ambition in your eyes. Hm. I could let it go for forty thousand gold...but gold alone won't earn my trust. If I sell it to you, I need proof you can be useful to me.

alkapoan_lie_wh_20.m: There's a small matter I want handled. Do this, and the price will stay at forty thousand. Refuse, and I'll reconsider whether you're worth the trouble.
r: What do you want from me?

alkapoan_lie_wh_30.m: If you want the house, I'll need proof that you can handle business my way. There's a card dealer who runs games in the back of the tavern here in Brimhaven. He operates because I allow it. That means he owes me a regular fee, call it an 'operation tax' if you will.

alkapoan_lie_wh_40.m: He's late. Bring me what he owes, and don't let him wiggle out of it. I want every bit of the five thousand gold. When you return with the gold, I'll know you're serious, and the deed will be yours for forty thousand more.
r: I'll be right back. Keep that deed handy.

alkapoan_lie_wh_50.m: Sure thing! As soon as I see forty-five thousand gold, you will see the deed to the house. Remember, you have my 'operation tax' gold too.
r: Forty-five thousand?! I don't have that kind of gold.
Here, take the fourty-five thousand and give me the deed and the key.

alkapoan_nocmar_wh_10.m: Ah...so this is for Nocmar? The man who couldn't pay his debt and lost everything. And now you want me to just hand it back? Hah! If he wants redemption, let him pay double what he owed. Fifty thousand gold, no less. You bring me that much, and I'll give you the deed and the key.
r: Fifty thousand gold?! Are you nuts? How about twenty-five housand?
Fifty thousand gold? I don't have it.
Here, take the fifty thousand and give me the deed and the key.

alkapoan_nocmar_wh_give_deed.m: A pleasure doing business with you.

alkapoan_not_enough_gold.m: Well, then you better go find it.

brv_guard_captain_15.m: Always stay on the right side of the law.

brv_guard_captain_20.m: Do you know anything about the destruction of the dam?
r: [Lie] I have no idea, but I will try to help you.
[Lie] The two brothers living in the north part of the eastern town destroyed the dam.
Alkapoan was behind it. Here are letters proving his guilt. He is waiting at his home for you to arrest him.

brv_guard_captain_22.m: You are accusing poor but honest people. Do you have any proof?
r: No, not yet, but I will try to help you.

brv_guard_captain_23.m: Come back when you have a proof, and until then stop accusing people. In the meantime, you are not allowed to leave the city.

brv_guard_captain_25.m: Hello again. Did you find out who destroyed the dam?
r: [Lie] The two brothers living in the north part of the eastern town destroyed the dam.
Alkapoan was behind it. Here are letters proving his guilt. He is waiting at his home for you to arrest him.

brv_guard_captain_30.m: We will check this and if it is true then you can leave the town.

brv_guard_captain_40.m: Thank you. But be aware that you are not allowed to leave the town until we have found out how the dam was destroyed.

brv_guard_captain_and_rich_man_10.m: [Laughs] You again. Welcome back, foolish child.
r: Laugh while you can. The captain is here and now you will get your deserved punishment!

brv_guard_captain_and_rich_man_30.m: Let's see who is laughing in the end. The captain came to talk, not arrest me. Now she owns a new horse and I will be earning a lot of money with the necessary repairing of the dam and later the food harvesting. I call this a win-win.

brv_guard_captain_and_rich_man_40.m: It seems Alkapoan's letters accidentally fell into a fire and I am sure some unknown evil spies from Loneford destroyed the dam. You better disappear soon, or I might find some evidence that you are the evil spy from Loneford.

brv_guard_captain_and_rich_man_50.m: You better disappear soon, or I might find some evidence that you are the evil spy from Loneford.
r: We are all reasonable people here. Let us settle this, shall we?
Oh, for the purposes of this conversation? Yeah, yeah I am. I want to talk to Alkapoan, not you!

talk_about_white_house_20.m: What do you want, foolish child?
r: I've collected your 'operation tax' from the dealer. Now let's finish our deal.
[lie] I want the glowing white house. I need a place to hide from my parents.
Nocmar has sent me to get back what was once his.

brv_flood.10: I found two not very bright brothers in a cellar of their house. They seemed to be talking about some sinister plan.
brv_flood.20: They were planning to destroy the great dam of Brimhaven. They just could not agree how they would do it.
brv_flood.30: They asked me to help them.
brv_flood.50: I have agreed to destroy the dam for them.
brv_flood.52: The brothers gave me a hand axe that could weaken the dam in a vulnerable place.
brv_flood.53: I took another hand axe. This time I shouldn't lose it.
brv_flood.54: I found the weak spot in the dam and started hacking at the wood.
brv_flood.56: Water came pouring through the hole in the dam. A lot of water!
brv_flood.70: I refused to destroy the dam for the brothers.
brv_flood.72: Given what I overheard, I was not allowed to leave. The two brothers attacked me.
brv_flood.80: Someone else destroyed the dam and water came pouring through a hole in the dam. A lot of water!
brv_flood.100: The Brimhaven guards have informed me that I may not leave the town until they have investigated who destroyed the dam.
brv_flood.110: I have promised to track down the real perpetrators. However, I still cannot leave the town.
brv_flood.120: The two brothers did not know their boss's name, but he seemed to have a lot of gold.
brv_flood.130: The rich man living up on the hill of Brimhaven seemed to know more than he admitted.
brv_flood.150: The rich man boasted that he had been bribed by an important man in Loneford to sabotage the dam.
brv_flood.200: I gave the letters as a piece of evidence to the captain of the guard. Now it is up to them to deal with the rich man.

place_to_forge.10: Nocmar refused to forge heartsteel in his shop, fearing discovery by Geomyr's men. He revealed that he once owned a glowing white house south of Fallhaven, where a special forge still burns. That forge was the only place he ever worked heartsteel. But after falling into debt, he lost the house to Alkapoan. If Nocmar is to forge again, I must help him regain it.
place_to_forge.20: Nocmar told me that Alkapoan holds the deed and key to the glowing white house. He said the forge within never dies, always blazing, ready for work. If I can reclaim the deed and key from Alkapoan, Nocmar will finally have his forge back.
place_to_forge.30: Alkapoan scoffed when I mentioned Nocmar. He said the only way to reclaim the glowing white house is to pay him fifty thousand gold. Nothing else will satisfy him.
place_to_forge.35: I told Alkapoan I wanted the glowing white house for myself. He agreed to sell it for forty thousand gold, but only if I first complete a task for him to prove my worth.
place_to_forge.40: Alkapoan asked me to collect an overdue 'operation tax' of five thousand gold from a card dealer in the back room of Brimhaven's tavern. I'll need to go there and retrieve the gold for Alkapoan before he will sell me the deed to the white house for forty thousand.
place_to_forge.45: I was able to collect the overdue 'operation tax' from the dealer and now I should return to Alkapoan.
place_to_forge.50: After I paid Alkapoan, he gave me the deed and the key to the white house south of Fallhaven. I should bring them back to Nocmar.
place_to_forge.60: I was able to finally give Nocmar back what was rightfully his...possession of his forge house.
